# Brave Free Origin - what every setting does

This is the complete list of what Brave Free Origin v2.0.2 can change: **101 Brave policies** on 12 pages, 6 presets, a DNS blocklist and the optional updater switches. Everything here is reversible: unticking a row and pressing **Apply** removes it, and **Restore stock** removes everything the tool ever set.

> **Checked against Brave 154.1.96.59 (Chromium 154) on 2026-09-29.** Brave adds, renames and retires policies over time. On a newer Brave a few rows may be renamed or gone (Brave ignores a policy it does not know, so nothing breaks); on an older one some rows may not exist yet. Open `brave://policy` to see exactly what your Brave accepted.

## How to read the tables

- **Ticked** means this tool enforces the row. For most rows that switches a feature **off** (the title says so: "Turn off ..."). Rows marked **keeps on** lock a protection Brave already uses by default, so nothing can silently weaken it. Rows marked **sets** write a specific value.
- **Unticked** means BFO requests that policy be absent. If the current value was recorded as BFO-owned it is removed directly; if it was not recorded as BFO-owned, Apply shows it first and asks before removing it.
- **Set elsewhere** means the policy already exists but BFO did not record writing that exact value. It is left alone until you deliberately change that row. Apply asks before replacing or removing it; keeping it restores the row to the state that was loaded from the PC.
- **Data-loss warning:** applying **Forget site data when a tab closes** or **Block custom New Tab backgrounds** can erase site data or saved customization. Apply shows a second warning and lets you unselect those settings while continuing with the rest.
- **Risk** says what an everyday user could lose: *Safe* and *Low* are fine for everybody; *Medium* and *High* change how Brave behaves, so read the description first.
- **Policy** is the registry value name under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\BraveSoftware\Brave` (one key for Stable, Beta, Nightly and Dev). It is also the name you will see in `brave://policy`.
- The preset columns show which presets tick the row: **Quick** = Quick Debloat, **Rec.** = Recommended, **Origin** = Origin Mode, **Boost** = Privacy + Boost, **Max perf.** = Max Performance, **Max priv.** = Max Privacy.

## Presets

A preset only ticks boxes; nothing is written until you press **Apply**. Presets never touch the updater switches, the search engine / new tab / startup overrides or the scriptlet tool.

| Preset | What it does | Risk | Policies ticked | Hosts groups ticked |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| **Quick Debloat** | Switches off Brave's six loudest extras: Rewards, Wallet, VPN, Leo AI, News and Talk. Nothing else changes. | Low risk | 6 | 3 |
| **Recommended** | Quick Debloat plus telemetry off, Chromium's AI and promo features off, and Brave's protections locked on. Passwords, autofill, sync, updates and session restore are left alone. | Low risk | 42 | 7 |
| **Origin Mode** | The free, local version of Brave Origin's idea: no Leo, Rewards, Wallet, VPN, News, Talk, Tor, Wayback Machine, Playlist, Speedreader, Email Aliases or usage analytics, with Shields kept strong. | Low risk | 16 | 6 |
| **Privacy + Boost** | Origin Mode and Recommended together, plus Memory Saver, Battery Saver, no background running, no Cast and no Live Caption download. A lighter browser for gaming, streaming or low-power laptops. | Medium risk | 54 | 7 |
| **Max Performance** | Privacy + Boost, plus a blank new tab and home page, a fresh start on every launch (no session restore) and a smaller disk cache. The plainest, fastest Brave. | Medium risk | 61 | 7 |
| **Max Privacy** | Recommended plus strict privacy: no sign-in, sync or imports, no autofill or password prompts, HTTPS only, and site data is forgotten when a tab closes. Expect signed-out sites and extra clicks. | High risk | 73 | 8 |
| **Stock / None** | Stock Brave. Nothing is ticked, so Apply removes everything this tool set and hands control back to Brave. | No changes | 0 | 0 |

## Shields and tracking

Brave's built-in tracking protection. Most of it is already on; ticking locks it so nothing can weaken it later.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Keep ad blocking on | Sets Shields' default to "Block ads and trackers" and stops the global default being changed to "Allow". Brave already blocks by default; ticking locks it. | `DefaultBraveAdblockSetting` | `2` (protection on, already Brave's default) | Low |  | x |  | x | x | x |
| Keep fingerprint protection on | Locks fingerprinting protection to Standard, which makes it harder for sites to recognise your browser by its unique traits. Brave's default; a few captchas and web apps may misbehave. | `DefaultBraveFingerprintingV2Setting` | `3` (protection on, already Brave's default) | Low |  | x |  | x | x | x |
| Limit the referrer sent to sites | Limits the "Referer" header to your site's origin for cross-site requests, so other sites do not see the full address you came from. Brave does this by default; ticking locks it. | `DefaultBraveReferrersSetting` | `2` (protection on, already Brave's default) | Low |  | x |  | x | x | x |
| Strip tracking codes from links | Removes known tracking codes (such as fbclid) from links when Shields is on. On by default; ticking locks it on. Rarely, a link that needs such a code stops working. | `BraveTrackingQueryParametersFilteringEnabled` | `1` (protection on, already Brave's default) | Low |  | x |  | x | x | x |
| Skip Google AMP pages | Opens the publisher's real page instead of Google's AMP copy, which limits tracking. Brave does this by default; ticking locks it on. | `BraveDeAmpEnabled` | `1` (protection on, already Brave's default) | Low |  | x |  | x | x | x |
| Skip tracker redirects | Sends you straight to your destination when a link goes through a known tracking redirect. On by default; ticking locks it on. Rarely, a redirect-based login can behave differently. | `BraveDebouncingEnabled` | `1` (protection on, already Brave's default) | Low |  | x |  | x | x | x |
| Always send "Do Not Sell" (GPC) | Tells websites you do not want your data sold or shared (Global Privacy Control). On by default; ticking locks it on. | `BraveGlobalPrivacyControlEnabled` | `1` (protection on, already Brave's default) | Safe |  | x |  | x | x | x |
| Hide language details from sites | Limits what sites can learn from your language settings, which makes fingerprinting harder. On by default; ticking locks it on. A few multilingual sites may pick a default language. | `BraveReduceLanguageEnabled` | `1` (protection on, already Brave's default) | Low |  | x |  | x | x | x |
| Require HTTPS (Strict) | Upgrades every link to HTTPS and shows a warning page instead of opening a site that has no HTTPS. Old routers, NAS boxes and local http:// pages need extra clicks or will not open. | `DefaultBraveHttpsUpgradeSetting` | `2` (value set) | Medium |  |  |  |  |  | x |
| Forget site data when a tab closes | Deletes a site's cookies and storage when you close its tab, so you are signed out of sites all the time and lose saved site settings. Brave normally keeps them. | `DefaultBraveRemember1PStorageSetting` | `2` (value set) | High |  |  |  |  |  | x |

Usage statistics, crash reports and remote experiments. Ticking stops the data from being sent.

| Setting | What it does | Policy | Writes | Risk | Quick | Rec. | Origin | Boost | Max perf. | Max priv. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |

| Turn off the usage ping | Stops the small daily ping that lets Brave count active users. | `BraveStatsPingEnabled` | `0` (feature off) | Safe |  | x | x | x | x | x |
| Keep Web Discovery off | The Web Discovery Project anonymously shares data to help build Brave Search. It is opt-in and off by default; ticking makes sure it stays off. | `BraveWebDiscoveryEnabled` | `0` (feature off, already Brave's default) | Safe |  | x | x | x | x | x |
| Turn off crash and usage reports | Stops Chromium's usage statistics and crash reports from being sent. Brave then gets no crash data from you, which can slow down bug fixes. | `MetricsReportingEnabled` | `0` (feature off) | Low |  | x |  | x | x | x |
| Turn off "Send feedback" | Removes the "Send feedback" option that can attach diagnostics to a report. | `UserFeedbackAllowed` | `0` (feature off) | Safe |  | x |  | x | x | x |
| Stop "make searches better" sharing | Prevents the addresses of pages you visit from being sent to Google to "make searches and browsing better". It is opt-in; ticking makes sure it cannot be enabled. | `UrlKeyedAnonymizedDataCollectionEnabled` | `0` (feature off, already Brave's default) | Safe |  | x |  | x | x | x |
| Block WebRTC log uploads | Stops services such as Google Meet from collecting WebRTC diagnostic logs from your browser. Brave already blocks this; ticking locks it. | `WebRtcEventLogCollectionAllowed` | `0` (feature off, already Brave's default) | Safe |  | x |  | x | x | x |
| Turn off remote experiments | Variations let Brave switch features on or off remotely (experiments, staged rollouts, kill switches). Ticking blocks all of them, so you only get built-in defaults - which can delay remote fixes. | `ChromeVariations` | `2` (value set) | Medium |  |  |  |  |  | x |
| Hide your local network address (WebRTC) | Websites can normally learn your device's local network address through WebRTC. Ticking limits WebRTC to your public address only, which some video-call and peer-to-peer sites do not like. | `WebRtcIPHandling` | `"default_public_interface_only"` (value set) | Medium |  |  |  |  |  | x |

## Site permissions

Decide for every site at once instead of being asked. Ticking blocks the permission by default; sites that need it stop working.

| Setting | What it does | Policy | Writes | Risk | Quick | Rec. | Origin | Boost | Max perf. | Max priv. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Block sites from using USB devices | Websites can normally ask to talk to USB gadgets. Ticking answers "no" without asking. Web tools that flash or configure USB hardware stop working. | `DefaultWebUsbGuardSetting` | `2` (feature off) | Low |  |  |  |  |  | x |
| Block sites from using Bluetooth devices | Websites can normally ask to connect to nearby Bluetooth gadgets. Ticking answers "no" without asking. Web tools for Bluetooth hardware stop working; regular Windows Bluetooth (headphones, mice) is not affected. | `DefaultWebBluetoothGuardSetting` | `2` (feature off) | Low |  |  |  |  |  | x |
| Block sites from using serial ports | Websites can normally ask to open serial (COM) ports, for 3D printers or microcontrollers. Ticking answers "no" without asking. Web serial consoles and hardware flashers stop working. | `DefaultSerialGuardSetting` | `2` (feature off) | Low |  |  |  |  |  | x |
| Block sites from using HID input devices | Websites can normally ask to talk to game controllers, keyboards and macro pads directly. Ticking answers "no" without asking. Web configurators for such devices stop working. | `DefaultWebHidGuardSetting` | `2` (feature off) | Low |  |  |  |  |  | x |
| Block sites from reading motion sensors | Sites can read device motion, orientation and light sensors, which helps them fingerprint you. Ticking denies that by default. Some maps, 360 viewers and web games that react to tilt stop responding to motion. | `DefaultSensorsSetting` | `2` (feature off) | Low |  |  |  |  |  | x |
| Block sites from seeing when you are idle | Sites can ask to know when you step away from the computer. Ticking answers "no" for every site without asking. Chat and team apps can no longer show an automatic "away" status. | `DefaultIdleDetectionSetting` | `2` (feature off) | Safe |  |  |  |  |  | x |
| Block sites from listing your fonts | Your installed fonts are a fingerprinting signal. Ticking stops sites from asking to see them. Online design tools cannot use your installed fonts. | `DefaultLocalFontsSetting` | `2` (feature off) | Low |  |  |  |  |  | x |
| Block sites from seeing your monitors | Sites can ask about your screens and place windows across them. Ticking answers "no" without asking. Presentation and multi-monitor web apps lose that ability. | `DefaultWindowManagementSetting` | `2` (feature off) | Low |  |  |  |  |  | x |

| Always allow QUIC (HTTP/3) | Allows QUIC, the faster HTTP/3 web protocol. It is allowed by default, so ticking only locks it on. A few corporate firewalls block QUIC. | `QuicAllowed` | `1` (protection on, already Brave's default) | Safe |  |  |  |  |  |  |

## Performance and startup

Memory, battery, disk and what opens when Brave starts.

| Setting | What it does | Policy | Writes | Risk | Quick | Rec. | Origin | Boost | Max perf. | Max priv. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Turn on Memory Saver | Puts tabs you have not used for a while to sleep so their memory can be reused. They reload when you return to them. | `HighEfficiencyModeEnabled` | `1` (protection on) | Low |  |  |  | x | x |  |
| Use Battery Saver on low battery | Reduces animations and background work when a laptop is unplugged and the battery is low. Users cannot turn Battery Saver off. | `BatterySaverModeAvailability` | `1` (protection on) | Low |  |  |  | x | x |  |
| Set GPU hardware acceleration | Lets Brave use your graphics card to draw pages and decode video. On is Brave's default. Pick Off only to work around GPU driver glitches, artifacts or crashes - video and scrolling get slower. | `HardwareAccelerationModeEnabled` | `1 / 0` (you choose, already Brave's default) | Low |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Limit the disk cache to 250 MB | Caps how much disk space the page cache may use (250 MB). The limit is a hint, not exact, and heavy browsing re-downloads more files. | `DiskCacheSize` | `262144000` (value set) | Low |  |  |  |  | x |  |
| Start on the New Tab page | Brave normally continues where you left off. Ticking makes it always open the New Tab page instead, and you lose your tabs after a restart or crash. | `RestoreOnStartup` | `5` (value set) | Medium |  |  |  |  | x |  |
| Make new tabs blank | Every new tab opens an empty page instead of Brave's New Tab page (top sites, background, News). No favorites or search box on new tabs. | `NewTabPageLocation` | `"about:blank"` (value set) | Medium |  |  |  |  | x |  |
| Home page is not the New Tab page | Separates the Home page from the New Tab page, so the Home button opens its own address. Only matters when the Home button is shown. | `HomepageIsNewTabPage` | `0` (value set) | Safe |  |  |  |  | x |  |
| Set the Home page to blank | Makes the Home button open a blank page and stops it being changed. | `HomepageLocation` | `"about:blank"` (value set) | Safe |  |  |  |  | x |  |
| Hide the Home button | Removes the Home button from the toolbar. Brave hides it by default; ticking locks it hidden. | `ShowHomeButton` | `0` (feature off, already Brave's default) | Safe |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Hide the Labs button | Hides the Labs (experiments) button from the toolbar. Brave already does not show it; ticking locks it. | `BrowserLabsEnabled` | `0` (feature off, already Brave's default) | Safe |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Block custom New Tab backgrounds | Users can no longer set their own New Tab background, and a custom background already set is permanently deleted - removing this policy later does not bring it back. | `NTPCustomBackgroundEnabled` | `0` (feature off) | Medium |  |  |  |  |  |  |

## Interface clutter

Small interface features you can remove.

| Setting | What it does | Policy | Writes | Risk | Quick | Rec. | Origin | Boost | Max perf. | Max priv. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Turn off Live Caption | Turns off Live Caption, which creates on-device captions for audio and video and needs a speech-model download. Deaf and hard-of-hearing users lose automatic captions. | `LiveCaptionEnabled` | `0` (feature off) | Low |  |  |  | x | x |  |
| Turn off Google image descriptions | For screen-reader users: stops unlabeled images from being sent to a Google service to get automatic descriptions. Screen-reader users lose those descriptions. | `AccessibilityImageLabelsEnabled` | `0` (feature off, already Brave's default) | Low |  |  |  |  |  | x |
| Block media autoplay | Stops videos and audio from starting on their own. Sites need a click to play, so some previews and players wait for you. | `AutoplayAllowed` | `0` (feature off) | Low |  |  |  |  |  | x |
| Remove the Share button | Removes the Share menu from the address bar and the page right-click menu. | `DesktopSharingHubEnabled` | `0` (feature off) | Safe |  |  |  |  | x |  |
| Remove "Create QR code" | Removes "Create QR code for this page" from the address bar and the right-click menu. | `QRCodeGeneratorEnabled` | `0` (feature off) | Safe |  |  |  |  | x |  |
| Save downloads without asking | Downloads start at once into your Downloads folder instead of asking where to save each file. Unwanted downloads are less obvious. | `PromptForDownloadLocation` | `0` (feature off) | Low |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Hide the bookmarks bar | Hides the bookmarks bar under the address bar, and it cannot be shown again in Settings. | `BookmarkBarEnabled` | `0` (feature off) | Low |  |  |  |  |  |  |

## Search engine and startup

Choose the address-bar search engine and what opens on launch and on new tabs. Each section only applies when its box is ticked.

| Override | What it writes |
| --- | --- |
| Default search engine (address bar) | `DefaultSearchProviderEnabled`, `DefaultSearchProviderName`, `DefaultSearchProviderKeyword`, `DefaultSearchProviderSearchURL`, `DefaultSearchProviderSuggestURL` |
| New Tab page | `NewTabPageLocation` |
| On startup (what opens when you launch Brave) | `RestoreOnStartup` and `RestoreOnStartupURLs` |

These are off until you tick their box, presets never change them, and they win over the matching rows on the other pages.

## Hosts blocklist

A second line of defence: block Brave's telemetry domains at the Windows level. This page has its own Apply button and never runs from the main one.

| Group | What it blocks | Risk | Domains | Pre-ticked by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Brave usage analytics (P3A) | The servers that receive Brave's anonymous usage analytics (P3A). Pure telemetry, never needed by a feature. | Safe | `collector.bsg.brave.com`, `star-randsrv.bsg.brave.com` | Recommended, Origin Mode, Privacy + Boost, Max Performance, Max Privacy |
| Brave usage ping | The server behind Brave's anonymous daily usage ping. Pure telemetry. | Safe | `usage-ping.brave.com` | Recommended, Origin Mode, Privacy + Boost, Max Performance, Max Privacy |
| Brave crash reports | The server that receives Brave crash reports. Reports are only sent if you agreed to them; blocking it is a safety net. | Safe | `cr.brave.com` | Recommended, Privacy + Boost, Max Performance, Max Privacy |
| Web Discovery Project | Servers for the Web Discovery Project. It is opt-in and off by default; blocking them is a safety net. | Safe | `collector.wdp.brave.com`, `quorum.wdp.brave.com`, `patterns.wdp.brave.com`, `star.wdp.brave.com` | Recommended, Origin Mode, Privacy + Boost, Max Performance, Max Privacy |
| Brave Rewards servers | Servers for Brave Rewards. Block them only if you do not use Rewards - it stops working if you turn it back on. | Low | `api.rewards.brave.com`, `rewards.brave.com`, `grant.rewards.brave.com` | Quick Debloat, Recommended, Origin Mode, Privacy + Boost, Max Performance, Max Privacy |
| Brave Ads servers | Servers for Brave Ads. Block them only if Rewards is switched off - Ads stop working if you turn Rewards back on. | Low | `anonymous.ads.brave.com`, `mywallet.ads.brave.com`, `geo.ads.brave.com`, `static.ads.brave.com`, `ohttp.ads.brave.com`, `search.anonymous.ads.brave.com` | Quick Debloat, Recommended, Origin Mode, Privacy + Boost, Max Performance, Max Privacy |
| Brave News servers | The servers behind the News feed and its images. Block them only if News is switched off - it stops working if you turn it back on. | Low | `brave-today-cdn.brave.com`, `pcdn.brave.com` | Quick Debloat, Recommended, Origin Mode, Privacy + Boost, Max Performance, Max Privacy |
| Brave experiments (Variations) | The server that sends Brave remote experiments and kill switches. Matches the Max Privacy setting that turns experiments off. | Medium | `variations.brave.com` | Max Privacy |
| Component and extension updates | The servers Brave's Shields filter lists, extensions and Tor come from. Blocking them freezes ad blocking, Widevine and extension updates. Experts only - never needed for privacy. | High | `go-updater.brave.com`, `componentupdater.brave.com`, `extensionupdater.brave.com`, `crxdownload.brave.com`, `brave-core-ext.s3.brave.com`, `redirector.brave.com`, `tor.bravesoftware.com` | no preset |

The hosts file matches exact names only (no wildcards), so this is a second line of defence behind the policies above. Only the block between the `# === Brave-Free-Origin START` and `# === Brave-Free-Origin END ===` lines is ever edited; everything else in the file is preserved byte for byte, and a backup is saved first.

## Updater tasks and services

Advanced. Only for people who update Brave by hand. Presets never change this page.

> Turning these off stops Brave from updating itself, so it will no longer get security fixes unless you update it by hand (Brave menu > About Brave). Only do this if you know why. Presets never touch this page.

| Item | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Stop the updater's scheduled check (scheduled task `BraveSoftwareUpdateTask*Core*`) | Brave's updater wakes up on a schedule to look for a new version. Turning it off means no automatic updates. |
| Stop the updater's version check (scheduled task `BraveSoftwareUpdateTask*UA*`) | The scheduled task that actually checks for and downloads new Brave versions. |
| Brave Update Service (Windows service `brave`) | The main background service of Brave's updater. |
| Brave Update Service (on demand) (Windows service `bravem`) | The on-demand helper of Brave's updater. |
